subject.title: ci: harden HTTP and local-auth gates against transient failures

question: Should this remain one umbrella CI-hardening issue, or should maintainers split the HTTP fixture and local-auth saturation work into independently owned fixes with separate acceptance checks?
rationale: The failures are independently actionable, while the local-auth path also requires a cost and capacity choice between runner provisioning and reducing application/test load.

options.title: Split into two focused tracks
options.body: Keep this issue as the evidence umbrella but implement and validate the HTTP fixture and local-auth saturation fixes independently.

options.title: Prioritize local-auth capacity first
options.body: Verify and correct actual runner quota before changing profile queries or retry behavior, leaving HTTP hardening as later follow-up.

options.title: Keep one combined implementation
options.body: Assign one owner to address both gates together and prove them with a unified repeated-run campaign.

recommendation.title: Split into two focused tracks
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the evidence umbrella but implement and validate the HTTP fixture and local-auth saturation fixes independently.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work owns the closest CI workflow and local-auth runner configuration history.
